request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "My crew due total" (`my-crew-due-total`). It adds up the due-totals of every crew led by the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user, and it's blank if that person leads no crew or no person matches. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in the front end; the server, stored data and audit records were not touched:

- **`features/crews/crews.ts`**: I moved the existing per-crew due-total sum into an exported `crewDueCents` function, so the crew rows and the header use the same rule: lead and members added up, anyone showing n/a skipped. The crews list is now passed up to the page that contains this panel.
- **`features/people/people.ts`**: added the header field. It finds the signed-in user's person the same way "My due total" does, picks the crews whose lead is that person, and adds their totals.

If a crew's lead is also a member of another crew the user leads, their due-total counts in both crews' totals. That matches what the request literally says (add up the crews' due-totals), and the test expects it.
